data.title: Eight students arrested after morning brawl at Siam
data.description: Eight students were arrested after a fight between groups from two rival educational institutions broke out on the OneSiam Skywalk in Pathumwan district on Friday morning, leaving four people injured.

data.title: House passes B400bn loan decree
data.description: <p>The House of Representatives has approved an emergency decree authorising the Finance Ministry to borrow up to 400 billion baht to address the impact of the energy crisis and support the country's energy transition.</p>

data.title: Anutin unfazed by 'trespassing' threat
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has dismissed reports that Cambodia may seek legal action against him over his recent visit to Chong An Ma, a disputed border area in Ubon Ratchathani.</p>

data.title: Govt to host air mobility symposium
data.description: <p>Thailand will host the International Civil Aviation Organisation's (ICAO) Advanced Air Mobility Symposium in December, creating opportunities for investment, technology development and stronger global aviation cooperation.</p>

data.title: Julapun asks South Korea to ease curbs
data.description: <p>Thailand has asked South Korea to expand job opportunities for Thai workers and ease restrictions on seasonal workers amid concerns over labour shortages.</p>

data.title: Asia Era One seeks premature deal exit
data.description: <p>Asia Era One Co, a private-sector partner in the high-speed rail link project connecting three airports, has confirmed its request to terminate the contract and cancel its agreement to operate the Airport Rail Link, prompting the State Railway of Thailand (SRT) to seek an urgent solution, the Transport Ministry said.</p>

data.title: Govt urged to implement 'Line 43' in Thap Lan park
data.description: <p>The activist Thap Lan 43 Group is urging the government to resolve a long-running land dispute involving communities inside Thap Lan National Park by using "Line 43", a jointly surveyed boundary mapped out in 2000 to resolve overlapping claims.</p>

data.title: Kindergarten exams, rankings to end
data.description: <p>The Education Ministry has ordered schools nationwide to end competitive examinations and ranking systems for kindergarten students, citing the early childhood development law.</p>

data.title: PM mulls more arms for navy
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul yesterday inspected the Royal Thai Navy's combat readiness in the Gulf of Thailand and signalled the possible procurement of additional weapons and military equipment to replace ageing systems.</p>

data.title: Royal Irrigation Department steps up Chao Phraya monitoring as rain looms
data.description: <p>Royal Irrigation Department (RID) director-general Witthaya Kaewmee has ordered closer monitoring of water levels in the Chao Phraya River basin as more rain is forecast from Aug 29 to Sept 2.</p>

data.title: Siripong defends shift to EVs amid oil-cost concerns
data.description: <p>Deputy Transport Minister Siripong Angkasakulkiat has defended the government's plan to convert public-service vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs), saying the scheme could cut oil consumption by an estimated 212 million litres a year while reducing transport costs and dependence on imported fuel.</p>

data.title: Gold traders spared tax but more oversight urged
data.description: <p>The Finance Ministry has no immediate plan to tax gold trading but wants the Gold Traders Association to help strengthen oversight and prevent money laundering, a leading gold trader said.</p>

data.title: Speaker pressed over NACC panel
data.description: <p>The opposition has pressed House Speaker Sophon Zarum to disclose the names of an independent panel reviewing a request to investigate the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) over its dismissal of a complaint against former transport minister Saksayam Chidchob.</p>

data.title: Explosives used to rob gold store near Thai-Cambodian border
data.description: Sa Kaeo: Police launched a hunt on Thursday for a robber who used explosives to make off with gold goods from a shop in a Lotus's superstore located in tambon Banmai Nongsai of Aranya Prathet district.

data.title: More sparks fly over Senate collusion case
data.description: The controversy over the Election Commission’s investigation into alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election intensified on Thursday, with senators accusing opposition figures of pressuring the poll agency and prejudging the case.

data.title: No Thais reported hurt in Nepal landslides
data.description: There are no reports of Thai nationals being injured, killed or missing following devastating flash floods and landslides in Nepal, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

data.title: Ex-Pheu Thai candidate held in exam fraud case
data.description: A former Pheu Thai Party candidate has been arrested in Bangkok for allegedly soliciting money in exchange for helping candidates pass civil service exams in his home province of Si Sa Ket.

data.title: Army says 52 drug smugglers killed in North in past 10 months
data.description: Thai soldiers have killed 52 drug smugglers in northern border areas since Oct 1 last year, according to the commander of the Pha Muang Task Force.

data.title: Pattaya ready to welcome 5,000 US military personnel
data.description: Pattaya is looking forward to welcoming about 5,000 American military personnel who will arrive for long-overdue rest and relaxation next week.

data.title: E-waste found in six containers at Laem Chabang
data.description: Six of 10 suspicious containers inspected on Wednesday at Laem Chabang Port in Chon Buri were found to contain electronic circuit boards mixed in with cargo declared as aluminium scrap.

data.title: Royal cremation preparations continue
data.description: <p>The Interior Ministry is accelerating preparations for the royal cremation ceremony of Her Majesty Queen Sirikit The Queen Mother, including public sandalwood-flower offering ceremonies at 878 venues nationwide.</p>

data.title: Cyber police seize guns in online crackdown
data.description: <p>Cyber police have arrested 186 people and seized 228 firearms, 1,294 rounds of ammunition and an improvised explosive device in a nationwide crackdown on illegal online gun trading.</p>

data.title: Ministry readies 878 venues
data.description: <p>The Interior Ministry is accelerating preparations for the royal cremation ceremony of Her Majesty Queen Sirikit The Queen Mother, including public sandalwood-flower offering ceremonies at 878 venues nationwide.</p>

data.title: Nanotec aids locals with eye on herbal products
data.description: <p>The National Nanotechnology Centre (Nanotec) is supporting Thai entrepreneurs in developing high-value herbal products using advanced technology to tap growing emerging markets and increase market shares.</p>

data.title: DSI refers second Stark case to attorney-general
data.description: <p>The Department of Special Investigation (DSI) has referred a second money-laundering case involving Stark Corporation (STARK) to the Office of the Attorney-General (OAG), whose ruling will determine jurisdiction over the transfer of 743 million baht to Singapore.</p>

data.title: Court set to rule on ballot secrecy row
data.description: <p>The Constitutional Court will rule on Sept 28 on whether barcodes and QR codes printed on ballot papers used in the Feb 8 general election breached constitutional protections for secret voting.</p>

data.title: Senate probe leak sparks legal action
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Wednesday backed legal action against those responsible for leaking documents from an investigation into alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election.</p>

data.title: Vegetables pass formalin test after Chinese scare
data.description: <p>The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has found no formalin contamination in 42 vegetable samples tested in the wake of reports of formalin being used on Chinese cabbage.</p>

data.title: Thais 'lag in using AI for work'
data.description: <p>Thailand has the world's highest usage of Google's Gemini Nano Banana for image generation, indicating a high level of creativity among Thai users. However, the country still lags behind its neighbours in using AI to boost productivity and economic value.</p>

data.title: Task force denies helicopter shots
data.description: <p>The Narathiwat Task Force has rejected reports that troops fired an M16 rifle from a helicopter at a group of youths in Chanae district, saying personnel carried no weapons during the surveillance mission.</p>

data.title: B57bn sought for southern projects
data.description: <p>Nearly 200 projects worth more than 57 billion baht have been proposed by five southern border provinces ahead of next week's mobile cabinet meeting in Hat Yai district of Songkhla.</p>

data.title: PM urges focus on upskilling
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has called for closer Asean cooperation to upgrade workers' skills in response to rapid advances in artificial intelligence, the green economy and demographic change, while promoting an Asean Digital Skills Passport to facilitate cross-border employment.</p>

data.title: Cyber cops seize guns in online crackdown
data.description: <p>Cyber police have arrested 186 people and seized 228 firearms, 1,294 rounds of ammunition and an improvised explosive device in a nationwide crackdown on illegal online gun trading.</p>

data.title: Energy crisis 'drives loan'
data.description: <p>Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has defended the government's 400-billion-baht emergency loan decree as essential to economic security as the energy crisis pushes the current-account deficit towards 600 billion baht.</p>

data.title: Fake school shooting threat a cover for a late delivery
data.description: RATCHABURI - Officials closed a school serving 3,000 students on Wednesday after receiving a shooting threat, only to find out later that a sports day jersey supplier had used it to postpone a delivery.

data.title: Abhisit says borrowing B400 billion won’t spur growth
data.description: Democrat Party leader Abhisit Vejjajiva has outlined four reasons for rejecting an emergency decree authorising the government to borrow 400 billion baht, warning that its passage would do little to change Thailand’s economic growth prospects while leaving people exposed to an ongoing energy crisis.

data.title: Suvarnabhumi road maintenance to disrupt traffic
data.description: Suvarnabhumi airport in Bangkok has advised passengers to plan their journeys in advance and allow extra travel time as a maintenance project will block some traffic lanes to and from the passenger terminal from next Monday to April 7 of next year.
